definitions.gloss: honorific title; title of respect; form of address
definitions.explanation: A suffix or title added to a person's name to show respect or politeness, such as さん, {様|さま}, {先生|せんせい}, or {殿|どの}.

examples.japanese: ⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{敬称|けいしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけて→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please add an honorific title in the letter.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{様々|さまざま}→様々：01559_samazama⟧な{敬称|けいしょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。

⟦メール→メール：04435_meeru⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{敬称|けいしょう}{略|りゃく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{書|か}いてあって→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、⟦{初|はじ}めて→初めて：02932_hajimete⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{敬称|けいしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧べきだ。
examples.english: Even if it says 'titles omitted' in an email, you should use honorific titles with someone for the first time.

notes:
USAGE:
In Japanese, {敬称|けいしょう} covers name suffixes like さん, ⟦{様|さま}→様：01549_sama⟧, ⟦{君|くん}→〜君：01998_kun⟧, ちゃん, ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧, and {殿|どの}. The phrase {敬称|けいしょう}{略|りゃく} ("titles omitted") appears on letters, invitations, or lists where honorifics are intentionally left off for brevity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {敬称|けいしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧ (to add an honorific title)
- {敬称|けいしょう}{略|りゃく} (titles omitted)
- {敬称|けいしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{省|はぶ}く→省く：02398_habuku⟧ (to omit honorific titles)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{呼称|こしょう}→呼称：12126_koshou⟧: form of address — broader, includes any way of addressing someone
- {称号|しょうごう}: title, designation — for formal titles like academic degrees or ranks
- ⟦{肩書|かたが}き→肩書き：13909_katagaki⟧: title, position — for job titles and official positions
